durable-names, the first of the finding's three store defects. sealLocked publishes the sealed segment with fsatomic.Replace, MoveFileExW with MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH on Windows, before the journal is truncated, in place of os.Rename and a SyncDirectory that does nothing on Windows. PublishCheckpoint writes its documents with atomicfile.Write, flushes its momentum file and publishes its directory with fsatomic.Replace. TestEveryDurableRenameGoesThroughItsOwner refuses an os.Rename outside internal/fsatomic unless its file declares why its name need not survive a crash, seven files with ten sites, holds the store to the cutover's three, and finds a rename planted under another name for os. It fails with the seal's rename put back (4 renames, want the cutover's 3). No crash or power cut was run; crash-points tests the seal.

unwritten-tail, the finding's journal-tail defect. In the journal a frame that is zeros to the end of the file, or one whose trailer and everything after it are zeros, ends the journal at its last whole commit, as a cut frame did; so does a first frame of zeros after a seal (pendingRotation). Open, OpenReadOnly and Create open such a journal with its head intact, a writer cuts the tail and Store.TornTail says how much, which overgodb repair prints and the server logs. A tail that is not zeros still refuses, a sealed segment ending in zeros still refuses as torn, and a journal with no whole header and no sealed segment is started by a writer. TestAnUnwrittenTailEndsTheJournal holds each case and fails with either zero check undone; TestCompleteCorruptFrameRejected is unchanged. No power cut was run; whether NTFS leaves such a tail is the finding's hypothesis.

cutover-kill, the finding's cutover defect. Under the writer's lock, an open that would start a store at a name that holds none refuses when the name's directory holds a store a cutover moved aside (name.superseded-*), and names it, where Create had started an empty store at sequence 0 beside the commits. ReplaceStore names the store it moves aside with the same marker. TestAKillBetweenCutoverRenamesStartsNoEmptyStore moves a store aside as the cutover's first rename does: Create refuses naming it, leaves nothing at the name, Open refuses, and the store moved back opens at its head. It fails with the check undone (Create gave no error). The cutover's renames stay os.Rename, declared in TestEveryDurableRenameGoesThroughItsOwner.

crash-points, the finding's third closure criterion for crash points. The review's recorder and crash enumerator are ported: TestEveryDurableOperationIsACrashPoint rewrites the store's production files through go/ast in an overlay, so every durable call reaches a recorder only the crashpoints tag compiles, records a workload of 322 durable operations, holds the recorder to rebuilding the tree the workload left, and checks every distinct state a kill (526), a power loss on a journaled volume (616) and the Windows rename rule (137) leave against eleven promises; all hold. TestEveryDurableOperationCanFail refuses each of 351 operations once and from there on; all hold. Reverting 345a08a3d's anchor check gives 1,548 kill and 1,724 power-loss findings, the seal's bare rename 1,209 under the Windows rule, and the zero-tail check off 162 power-loss findings. The recovery model goes to the long run, as the row says. Retiring the old append seam and moving its four fault tests into the harness is filed as store-durability/fault-seam. The finding's lifecycle criterion is store-lifecycles, next.

store-lifecycles, the finding's lifecycle criterion. TestGeneratedStoreLifecycles drives 40 seeded lifecycles of 60 steps (commits, seals, closes leaving no, a few or any tail, opens, reads, releases, packs, repeats, stale heads) across two writers and a reader, each handle held after a refresh to a small reference of head and content bytes, and checks 6 sampled kill states of each against the crash harness's promises, under the crashpoints tag over the harness's overlay. Before the fix 31 of 40 lifecycles broke a promise through the stale pack index: absent blob, same length wrong bytes, a pack refused while reading its predecessor, bytes not hashing to their identity. The fix: blobPack keeps the file its index was read from, every lookup opens the pack and reads the index again when the opened file is another (os.SameFile on the handle's identity), and a read takes its offset from the index of the very file it reads; the packer's forget is gone. After: 0 of 40 in about 11 s, 0 of 200 in 25 s. The crash harness's crashShort now masks noise word by word, so a message is no longer written as a bare #. The remaining criterion is store-durability/fault-seam.

device_newton_schulz_normalization.assessment: All owner refinements were applied before the deciding comparison. Supported Windows/CUDA execution required OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1 and observed execution of both 8+2 FP32 and 4+2 TF32. The 514 scalar comparisons and 56 directions passed bitwise, including guard decisions, normalization multipliers, zero/tiny weights and thresholds around rounded FP32 squared norms. FP64 round-to-nearest scalar instructions were checked despite fast-math compiler options. Twelve alternating pairs across 32 cells compared preservation with reconstruction and counted bandwidth, launches and otherwise-skipped GEMMs. Normal cases ranged from no detectable gain to about 15% faster; every guarded cell was about 105-395% slower. The declared stopping rule rejected the candidate before further full-step/streamed runs. The unchanged production path remains. Optimizer-only gain could have qualified under the frozen 5% minimum, full-step regression and memory limits, but the guard-heavy limit failed. No candidate full-step improvement is claimed.

Paired outcomes were 15 reasoning-only, 5 direct-only and 20 ties; ExactPairedBinary tail 0.020694732666015625 is below the existing inclusive 0.0227501319482 threshold. Each arm had one unmatched answer. Four direct generations and no reasoning generations reached their respective generated-token limits. The historical 34/40 reasoning score did not reproduce; its full seed, source and environment provenance was unavailable. The sample remains exposed development evidence, not an independent held-out gain or a search budget. Existing sample, outcome and paired-statistics owners are reused with no new production/test code.
